Messages.Author: Francois Gombault
Messages.Body:
Here's a card suggestion. I like card suggestions. They are useless, and
allow us to discuss and insult each other for no real reason. :)

So, in a desperate attempt to make Deal with the Devil suck less, here is
:

Infernal Knowledge, Unique Master, Baali

Put Infernal Knowledge in play. You may pay 1 pool to play a card from you
ash heap as if it was from your hand. Cards played this way are removed
from the game instead of going to you ash heap. Any minion may burn
Infernal Knowledge as a (D) action.

3, 2, 1, let's flame !

Francois

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
"Henrik Isaksson" <hen...@nissamedia.net> wrote in message
news:a7filv$l58vk$1...@ID-135400.news.dfncis.de...

>
> I wonder if cardsuggestions like this makes it harder for poor White-Wolf??
> If they don't wan't to make cards that someone suggested, every suggestion
> restricts WW to one idea less to use... Or has there actually been any cases
> where cards suggested by newsgroups or fans have been printed?
>

FRPG used to have a policy that if a card idea was posted to any public forum,
they would never print a card like that. It was considered kind of silly
because a) they can't monitor *everywhere*, and b) what happened if someone
independently came up with an idea that they'd already made into an as yet
unreleased card?

WW has no such policy, AFAIK. That doesn't mean that they'll consider for
submission ideas that are posted to the newsgroup. They may well have some
internal policy not to consider that type of submission. In any case, most
design teams prefer to design their own cards and are somewhat closed to
suggestions.

I'm of the opinion that at least one card idea was ripped off (not that we
minded *at all*) from our online playtest set, headed up by Justin Fang and
including a number of people who still post on this newsgroup. The cards can
be found at www.ugcs.caltech.edu/~justinf/jyhad/ (the project was mostly
abandoned after WW took up the V:TES banner and started making cards again).
The list is somewhat long and ponderous, and I wouldn't recommend browsing
through the whole thing, but in particular, "Raise the Ancients" has exactly
the same text as Zillah's Valley. This could, of course, be coincidence, but i
don't think it is. (There were a few other cards that were similar to cards in
FN, but they could just be coincidence... we were drawing from the same
background material, after all.)

Chances are that WW is not completely deaf to card suggestions, but I wouldn't
hold your breath on seeing any particular idea in print.

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>I wonder though if "Baali" is a proper requirement; woulnd't "Requires
>a ready Infernal vampire" better? Else, as soon as someone Clan
>Impersonate a Baali, you could play the card.
>
>Unless, of course, if Impersonating a Baali makes you Infernal
>automatically... ?

No it doesn't. Unlike the Blood Curse, Infernal is not inherent to the clan
(it's possible to have a future Baali not be Infernal). Similarly, Sterility
and Cold Iron Vulnerability are not inherent to a clan and like Infernal, are
not passed down to Embraces (though the Sterility thing prevents you from
Embracing in the first place).

Halcyan 2

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>Hesha (follower of set 6 cap) is the only one that comes redily to mind at
>the moment, but there are others on there...
>

But then again, Hesha is a character from the RPG, whose stats and background
(including the part about owning a blood bank) are well-known and even
published on the web-site. So given, his character sheet, it's not all too hard
to come up with a reasonable (or even accurate) guess at his card
representation.

In addition, even if White Wolf did copy (without permission) a created
Jyhad/VTES vampire that someone else thought of, in many cases the third party
creates a representation of a character that is already in White Wolf's World
of Darkness. Since White Wolf created and pretty much owns the concept of
Marcus Vitel, if some person develops their own Marcus Vitel crypt card and
White Wolf copies it, it'll be an uphill battle to combat White Wolf over their
very own creation. IT might be interesting or amusing to revisit the little
"Camarilla" fiasco-thingy for the LARP...

Halcyan 2
